subject: maths
title: The quadratic formula and the discriminant

lines.say: Some quadratics, like x squared plus 5x plus 2, don't factorise neatly.
The quadratic formula is a master key. It solves every quadratic.
It comes from completing the square in general.
Write a, b and c first, with their signs. Here 1, 5 and 2.
Work out b squared minus 4ac first. 25 minus 8 is 17.
Substitute: minus 5, plus or minus root 17, all over 2.
The plus or minus gives two answers: about minus 0.44 and minus 4.56.
The whole top line is divided by 2a, not just the root.
Solve 2x squared minus 3x minus 4. b is minus 3, c is minus 4.
Minus 3, in brackets, squared is 9. Then minus 4 times 2 times minus 4 adds 32.
Minus b is plus 3. So x is 3 plus or minus root 41, over 4.
Simplify surds. 4 plus or minus root 20, over 2, becomes 2 plus or minus root 5.
The part under the root is the discriminant, delta.
Three parabolas that differ only in the constant term.

draw.alt: Three parabolas: crossing twice, touching once, not reaching the x-axis

lines.say: Delta positive: two solutions. The graph crosses twice.

draw.alt: Three parabolas: crossing twice, touching once, not reaching the x-axis

lines.say: Delta zero: one solution. The graph just touches.

draw.alt: Three parabolas: crossing twice, touching once, not reaching the x-axis

lines.say: Delta negative: no real solutions. The graph never reaches the axis.

Delta is 16 minus 28, which is minus 12.
Negative, so you can't take the square root. No real solutions.
If delta is a perfect square, the solutions are rational. It factorises.
Positive but not a perfect square? The answers contain a surd.
For which k does x squared plus kx plus 16 have one solution?
One solution means delta equals 0.
k squared minus 64 equals 0, so k is 8 or minus 8.
Check: x squared plus 8x plus 16 is x plus 4, all squared.
